<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>Circle</title>
  <style>
    *,
    *::before,
    *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }

    html,
    body {
      height: 100%;
    }

      justify-content: center;
      align-items: center;

      height: auto;
      aspect-ratio: 1 / 1;
    }

    circle {
      fill: #111;
    }

    @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
      body {
        background: #111;
      }
      circle {
        fill: #f5f5f5;
      }
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>

    <title id="circle-title">A solid circle</title>
    <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
I rewrote `0.html` with the same visual (a centered circle) and these improvements:

- **No stray scrollbars.** Replaced the 100vw/100vh body sizing, which triggers horizontal overflow when a scrollbar is present, with full-height html/body and overflow hidden.
- **Responsive circle.** The SVG now scales down on small screens instead of being fixed at 400px, while keeping a square aspect ratio.
- **Accessibility.** The SVG has an image role and a visible-to-screen-reader title, and the page title is descriptive instead of a hash.
- **Dark mode.** Background and circle colors swap under the system dark color scheme.
- **Housekeeping.** Added border-box sizing to the reset and moved the circle fill into CSS so it is easy to restyle.
